streams.activity: Reworking Nobuyuki's attack timing to match Samurai Warriors 4.
streams.description: Characters from other Warriors games, added as new playable characters. Nobuyuki Sanada is the first and is playable in testing. The rest of the list is a wishlist, so the overall figure stays low until more characters are started.

substreams.title: Nobuyuki Sanada
substreams.summary: Playable in testing with his Samurai Warriors 4 model, moves, cloth physics and all six weapons.
substreams.activity: Reworking his attack timing to match Samurai Warriors 4.
substreams.description: Nobuyuki is ported from Samurai Warriors 4. He has his own Samurai 4 tab on Character Select, cloth physics on his coat and ponytail, and all six weapons, including a sakura Mythic weapon and a black and crimson X weapon. His moveset is being rebuilt to match Samurai Warriors 4: the full normal string, charge attacks, Hyper attacks, jump attacks, Special Attack and the musou camera work in testing, and his attack timing is being reworked. His Special Attack will also push enemies back, as in Samurai Warriors 4. Still to come: his own character slot, his Gallery entry and a second outfit.

streams.title: Improved graphics
streams.summary: Smoother edges, stronger light shafts and sharper shadows work in game.
streams.activity: Studying how newer Warriors games render, to guide the next improvements.
streams.description: The mod uses its own graphics add-on. Smoother edges, stronger light shafts, sharper shadows and shadows from stage scenery work in game. Next, the way Samurai Warriors 5, Dynasty Warriors: Origins and Dynasty Warriors 3 Complete Edition Remastered draw their scenes is being studied to guide further improvements.

streams.title: Menu improvements
streams.summary: The menu scaling has been reworked, and menus hold up on 21:9 and 16:10 screens. Xbox, PlayStation 5 and Switch 2 button prompts are in.
streams.activity: Checking every menu screen at different screen sizes.
streams.description: Menus across the game have been rescaled to fit modern screens, including the Gallery screens. They have been tested at 16:9, 16:10 and 21:9. Button prompts for Xbox, PlayStation 5 and Switch 2 controllers have been added.

screenshots.alt: The Battle Preparations menu with its updated layout
screenshots.caption: The reworked Battle Preparations menu.

streams.title: Larger battles
streams.summary: Battles can hold up to 250 characters instead of 180, and soldiers now reappear out of the camera's view.
streams.activity: Checking how the new spawning feels in play.
streams.description: The game normally limits a battle to 180 characters, so soldiers disappear and reappear as others spawn. The limit is now 250, and a test battle reached 241. Characters are drawn further away, soldiers only reappear where the camera can't see them, and suspend saves keep the extra soldiers.

streams.title: Ultrawide screens
streams.activity: Working out what needs to change for ultrawide screens.
streams.description: Support for 21:9 and 32:9 displays across battles, menus, movies and loading screens. The first step is checking how each part of the game behaves on wider screens.

streams.title: Named officers become new characters
streams.summary: Named officers in battle, such as Nobuyuki Sanada, will appear as the new characters with their own model and moves.
streams.activity: Looking at how named officers are set up in the game data.
streams.description: Many stages have named officers who aren't playable, such as Nobuyuki Sanada. The plan is for them to appear as the new playable characters instead, with their own model and moveset. The game already does this for a few characters. This comes after the new character slots, since each new character needs a slot of their own first.
